raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Two bugs in GLM tool calling lose a call that the model tried to make. The cookbook uses `glm47` for GLM-4.7 through GLM-5.3.

**Repeated argument keys.** With the `glm47` or `flint` parser, one tool call can repeat argument keys until `max_tokens`, so the request returns no usable call. Any request with non-strict tools and `tool_choice` `auto` or `required` can reach this. On public GLM-4.7-Flash with a synthetic prompt, 234 of 432 requests hit the 4000-token limit on main and 0 of 432 with this PR. The prompt demands an argument that the schemas lack, and how often clients send this shape is not measured. In a smaller run of 160 requests, the loop needed the system prompt and history together: 20 of 32 on main with both, and 0 of 128 on main in the other scenarios. An ordinary prompt in that run also lost queries: in 4 of 32 requests to search five terms, the non-stream parser kept only the last of 5 or 6, and this PR returned 6 separate calls.

**Unserializable literals.** When a GLM model writes a tool argument as a Python set, bytes, or complex literal, main returns raw markup instead of the tool call. Chat completions streams end with no finish reason or `[DONE]`, and the server logs `TypeError: Object of type set is not JSON serializable`. `glm45` and `iquest_q1` can reach this on any non-string-typed parameter, because `tool_choice` auto has no grammar. `glm47` reaches it through a schema the grammar leaves free, such as `$ref`, or a client constraint. Every run prompted or forced the literal, so unprompted frequency is unmeasured and may be low. An issue search found no user report.

I found no other open PR that bounds these pairs or fixes this crash. #46672 bounds the text preamble. #43270 and #43264 conflict with this PR over a separate tuple bug. The second to land keeps both changes, with `json.dumps` before the tuple branch.

## Modifications

- Limit the argument pairs in each call to the number of keys in a complete schema. Keys stay optional and in any order. A closed schema with no keys allows no pairs.
- Check the literal result with `json.dumps` in the `glm45` and `glm47` parsers. If that fails, keep the original argument text, as the Poolside parser does. `iquest_q1` and `ling3` inherit this check.

Limits:

- With parallel tool calls on, repeated whole calls stay accepted.
- Incomplete or free-form schemas keep the unbounded rule.
- A repeated key can push out a later key.
- Requests with a strict tool skip this grammar.
- Where values stream verbatim, a Python literal still gives invalid JSON deltas: array, object, and boolean with `glm47`, and declared non-string types with `glm45`. Fixing this needs buffering. Open #43275 changes these `glm47` deltas.
- `{'a': 1e999}` gives non-standard `Infinity`.

## Accuracy Tests

This commit combines the diffs of PR heads `2a8e438c78` (repeated keys) and `9cc39c115d` from closed #44111 (literals), squashed onto main `7b88f09239`. The squash kept both diffs, and no run below used it. On the squashed commit, only pre-commit and the function-call parser and GLM schema unit test modules ran, on CPU, and the test modules found no failure.

Repeated-key runs used the diff of `2a8e438c78`. Literal runs used `a94b1b8d59` and `9cbf72e162` (`9cc39c115d` is its cherry-pick), as #44111 records for each row. No server ran both fixes. A CPU suite on main `99fd01047d` merged both fixes with other PRs. It failed only in files that also fail on main, plus `test_kv_events` with `Address already in use`, which its main run did not hit but a separate record shows in 18 of 20 runs on main.

Repeated keys, with the cookbook command and these settings:

```text
main: 582168dd7c
repeated-keys tree: 582168dd7c plus the diff of PR head 2a8e438c78
server, per tree, 1 B200: python -m sglang.launch_server --model zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tp 1 --attention-backend triton --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45
requests: non-stream with logprobs, temperature 0, 0.7, and 1.0, thinking on and off, max_tokens 4000, 16 concurrent, no pinned seed
tools: 192 requests with 4 tools including a closed no-argument tool and tool_choice auto, 48 with the same 4 tools and tool_choice required, 192 with only a one-key tool and tool_choice auto
scenario: system prompt requires a telemetry argument, history holds calls with it, tool schemas lack it
smaller live run: same trees and server, temperature 0 and 0.7 only, the same 4 tools with tool_choice auto, 160 requests over 5 prompt scenarios
later live repeat: main ba1ed00dfe plus the same diff, same server, 48 requests in each tool group (144 total), then the 8 streaming requests
```

| Check | Main | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live, requests with `finish_reason` `length` | 234 of 432 | 0 of 432 |
| Live, requests with no parsed tool call | 234 | 0 |
| Live, most argument pairs in one call | 666 | 3 |
| Live, most whole calls in one request | 12 | 5 (five different queries) |
| Live, total completion tokens | 967,628 | 25,841 |
| Live, client wall time | 919 s | 46 s |
| Later live repeat, reduced matrix, `finish_reason` `length` | 80 of 144 | 0 of 144 |
| Later live repeat, 8 streaming requests with a one-key tool, thinking off, temperature 0.7, `finish_reason` `length` | 6 of 8 | 0 of 8 |
| Later live repeat, the same streaming requests, valid JSON arguments | 2 of 8 | 8 of 8 |
| XGrammar mask once a call reaches its limit | `<arg_key>` allowed | `<arg_key>` removed, `</tool_call>` kept |
| XGrammar mask after the tool name, closed no-argument schemas | `<arg_key>` allowed | `<arg_key>` removed |
| XGrammar mask after the tool name, `{"type": "object", "properties": {}}` | `<arg_key>` allowed | `<arg_key>` allowed |
| llguidance, one pair over the limit, with ordinary tokens that spell the tags, because it rejects the `<tool_call>` special token on both trees | Accepted | Rejected |
| 200 repeated whole calls with parallel tool calls on | Accepted | Accepted |
| Repeated key in parser output (the parser does not change) | Plain streaming sends both pairs. Non-streaming and union schemas keep the last value. | Same |

The XGrammar, llguidance, repeated-call and parser rows ran at `2a8e438c78` (on main `c757c4bb7c`) on CPU, with the GLM-5.3-Flash tokenizer.

Literals, on one B200. The first four rows had no client constraint and a prompt that asked for the literal. In the `glm45` row, that prompt followed one earlier tool call. In the last row, a client `ebnf` forced the values. The full matrix is in closed #44111.

| Parser and weights | Case | Main | With the fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `glm47`, GLM-4.7-Flash, `$ref` object | Set literal, non-streamed | Call dropped, raw markup as content, finish reason `stop` | Raw text as a string argument, finish reason `tool_calls` |
| Same | Same input, streamed | No finish reason, no `[DONE]`, `TypeError` in the server log | Finish reason `tool_calls`, `[DONE]`, no error in the log. Deltas stay invalid JSON, as on main |
| `glm45`, GLM-4.7-Flash weights with the `zai-org/GLM-4.5` chat template | Array parameter, set literal, non-streamed and streamed | Same failures as the two rows above | Same results as the two rows above |
| `iquest_q1`, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct | Plain array, non-streamed and streamed | Call dropped non-streamed. Stream ends with no finish reason or `[DONE]` | Finish reason `tool_calls` with valid JSON in both modes |
| `glm47` and `iquest_q1` on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, `glm45` on GLM-4.7-Flash weights with the `zai-org/GLM-4.5` chat template | Valid `[1, 2]` and `5` | Normal tool call | Same output |

The new grammar and literal tests fail on main.

Not run: a replay of production requests, the repeated-keys fix on any model other than GLM-4.7-Flash (including `flint`), GLM-4.5, GLM-4.6, GLM-5.x, Ling-3, or IQuest-Q1 weights, llguidance on a live server, `/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages` with `glm47`, `glm47` grammar routes other than `$ref` on a server, any test or server on `9cc39c115d`, a server with both fixes, and runtime CI (no `run-ci` label).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Grammar work only, on the XGrammar compile, on CPU with the GLM-5.3-Flash tokenizer at `2a8e438c78` (on main `c757c4bb7c`), median of three. Median per-token mask time stayed at 1 to 2 microseconds. The serialization check runs only after JSON parsing fails.

| Compile | Main | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 50 tools with 30 keys | 557 ms, 2.67 MB | 559 ms, 3.14 MB |
| 1 tool with 300 keys | 360 ms, 0.63 MB | 360 ms, 0.68 MB |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+        # A repeated key must not let one call grow until max_tokens.
+        for keys in (["query"], ["query", "from", "to"]):

+                "".join(pairs): True,

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cap arguments for complete zero-key schemas**

When a no-argument tool declares `{"properties": {}, "additionalProperties": false}`, `_glm_has_complete_properties()` regards it as complete but `all_props` is empty, so this new bounded rule is skipped and the fallback `(...)*` still accepts arbitrary repeated argument pairs. Such GLM47 calls can therefore still run to `max_tokens`, precisely the production loop this change is meant to prevent; distinguish a complete empty schema from an unresolved/free-form schema and emit zero argument pairs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
